 Students hoping to secure money for college could face financial aid deadlines months before the federal government stops accepting applications, but it depends on where they live. The 2027-28 Free Application for Federal Student Aid, better known as the FAFSA, is now available, allowing students to apply for grants, scholarships, work-study opportunities and federal student loans. While the federal FAFSA deadline is not until June 30, 2028, individual states and colleges often impose much earlier deadlines, and much of the money available is distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. California's deadline for most state financial aid programs is March 2, 2027, for instance, while Arizona gives students seeking priority consideration for its Promise Program until April 1. Why It Matters The FAFSA is one of the most important steps students can take to reduce what they have to pay for college. Colleges use information from the application to determine eligibility for financial aid, which can include grants and scholarships that do not generally have to be repaid, as well as work-study opportunities and student loans. Map Shows FAFSA Deadlines Across the U.S. Deadlines vary substantially by program and location. Some states specify a calendar date while others merely have priority deadlines. For the 2027-28 cycle, California has a March 2 deadline for most state financial aid programs. Other states with deadlines before or by March include Arkansas, Idaho, Maryland, West Virginia, Texas, Connecticut, Louisiana and Missouri. Other states stipulate that you should apply as soon as possible because funds remain limited and are given out on a first-come, first-served basis. That includes Alaska, Georgia, Illinois, Kentucky, Montana, Nevada, North Carolina, North Dakota, Oregon, South Carolina, Vermont, Virginia and Washington. Experts say missing a state deadline does not mean a student should give up on FAFSA because they’ll still generally qualify for federal student aid, even if state funds run out. “The main emphasis this year is the importance of applying early, especially at the state level, where financial aid may be limited,” Kevin Thompson, the CEO of 9i Capital Group, told Newsweek. “The longer you wait, the greater the possibility that available funding could be exhausted.” When Is the Federal FAFSA Deadline? For students seeking aid for the 2027-28 academic year, the FAFSA is due by 11:59 p.m. CT on June 30, 2028. Corrections or updates must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. CT on September 12, 2028. The June 2028 date is not, however, when students should apply; it is the final federal cutoff. Applying earlier is better because students can feel more financially secure entering the school year. “Many states and colleges have much earlier deadlines, and waiting too long could equate to missing out on thousands of dollars in grants and scholarships that don’t have to be repaid,” Alex Beene, a financial literacy instructor at the University of Tennessee at Martin, told Newsweek. How Students Can Get Financial Aid Students can complete the FAFSA online through StudentAid.gov. The government says applicants typically finish their portion of the form in 12 minutes or less, but parents or spouses may also have information they need to provide. Before starting, students should have their verified StudentAid.gov account credentials, or FSA ID, along with relevant income and asset information. Getting the application in early can be especially important for programs with limited pools of grant or scholarship money. “Two students with similar financial circumstances could receive very different aid packages simply because of where they attend college and when they apply,” Beene said. “This year’s FAFSA is available earlier than in some recent application cycles and includes clearer questions, improved communication options for parents and other contributors, and additional fraud protections, but my advice remains the same, which is to apply as early as possible.” What Students Should Do After Filing FAFSA Submitting the form is not necessarily the final step. Students should monitor their FAFSA account, email and college financial aid portals in case additional documentation or corrections are required. Errors can delay an aid package, and making corrections after a state or institutional deadline could affect eligibility for some programs. Students should also remember that the FAFSA is not a college's final financial aid offer. “FAFSA uses your family's 2025 income. What if a parent lost their job in 2026? Your application could make your family look much better off financially than it is today,” Michael Ryan, a finance expert and the founder of MichaelRyanMoney.com, told Newsweek. “I'd file early. Then ask the college for a 'financial aid adjustment' if your circumstances have changed. Don't assume the numbers on an old tax return tell your whole financial story.” What Happens Next Students planning to attend college, graduate school or an eligible career school during the 2027-28 academic year can file the FAFSA now. Because the federal, state and individual school deadlines can differ, students should check all three. However, filing as early as possible is best for a better chance of being considered for state and institutional programs with limited funding.
